title: Minimal Scenarios Witnessing Genuine Multipartite Nonlocality Possibilistically
abstract: We study a strong form of genuine multipartite nonlocality (GMNL), where an $n$-partite scenario admits a quantum strategy generating outcomes belonging to a restricted set with certainty, whereas every strategy built from nonclassical resources shared among at most $k<n$ parties fails this criterion with positive probability. This generalizes what is referred to as strong contextuality/nonlocality, or pseudotelepathy, beyond ruling out local models. For the simplest five-party Bell scenario of two binary-outcome measurement settings per party, we use the inflation technique to demonstrate that a game with a perfect quantum strategy witnesses a robust separation from models built from bipartite resources under local operations and shared randomness (LOSR), establishing the behavior is LOSR-GMNL. We provide broader context for this result by investigating its simulability with resources shared among three or four parties under different resource models and alternative definitions of GMNL. A central open question is whether $n$-party quantum resources can achieve such a separation from models built from $(n-1)$-party resources, for $n\ge 3$. We make progress here by constructing a family of robustly LOSR-GMNL games with $ε$-optimal quantum strategies experimentally indistinguishable in the limit from true probability-one-winning strategies for any desired level of precision.
summary: This work establishes strong quantitative bounds on genuine multipartite nonlocality using the inflation technique applied to multi-party Bell-type games. By showing that certain quantum correlations cannot be simulated by any network of fewer parties, it advances the understanding of the fundamental resource requirements for quantum information protocols.
main_problem: The paper investigates a strong form of genuine multipartite nonlocality (GMNL) to determine the minimum number of parties required to witness correlations impossible for models based on fewer parties.
main_result: The authors demonstrate robustly LOSR-GMNL behavior for the 5-party Bell scenario using an inflation technique, establishing a separation from models built from bipartite resources.
method: The primary methods involve using the inflation technique to derive robust separation bounds and analyzing the constraints imposed by the no-signaling principle on correlated binary random variables.
model_or_system: The study focuses on nonlocal games, specifically the 5-party Bell scenario (5 parties, two binary-outcome measurements per party), and generalizes this analysis to arbitrary $n$-party systems.
key_observables: Winning probability of the nonlocal game; the separation factor between quantum predictions and the bound derived from bipartite resources.
important_parameters: The number of parties ($n$), the resource model (e.g., bipartite vs. $n$-partite), and the precision parameter $\epsilon$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies heavily on the no-signaling principle and the application of the inflation technique to relate probabilities across different resource ancestries.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the pairwise-resource network for the 5-cycle game and its two-copy non-fanout inflation used in bounding the winning probability.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining strong GMNL, applying the inflation technique to the 5-party game to derive quantitative bounds, and then generalizing the mathematical framework to construct families of robustly LOSR-GMNL games for arbitrary $n$.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical techniques used to quantify the resource requirements for genuine multipartite entanglement and nonlocality are foundational to understanding quantum correlations beyond simple entanglement measures.
